sections.content:
48,025 people

were counted on the census as "registered nurse practitioners" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Registered nurse practitioners provide nursing care for the sick, injured and others in need of care, assist medical doctors with their tasks and also provide care independently, including diagnosing patients, ordering and interpreting tests, deciding treatment and prescribing medication.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "registered nurse practitioners", 14.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "registered nurse practitioners" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "registered nurse practitioners" included:

  • social services managers and directors
  • skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades supervisors
  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "registered nurse practitioners" there were more women than men (79.8% compared with 20.2%).

This means "registered nurse practitioners" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "health professionals".

Men made up 20.2% and women made up 79.8% of "registered nurse practitioners"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "registered nurse practitioners" included:

  • hairdressing and beauty salon managers and proprietors
  • psychotherapists and cognitive behaviour therapists
  • librarians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "registered nurse practitioners", 11.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (72.8% compared with 27.2%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.9%) than self-employed (4.1%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
